label: December 29–January 04
title: The First Testament of Jesus Christ —  Introduction to the

items.text: The Old Testament, while ancient and sometimes seemingly foreign, contains familiar human experiences and gospel themes that testify of Jesus Christ's divinity. Like Abraham, Sarah, and Daniel, we face joys, discord, faith, uncertainty, successes, and failures, but also exercise faith, repent, make covenants, and never give up on the Savior’s promise.

As we learn how God moved in the lives of ancient peoples, we can also see Him in our own lives. The psalmist declared, 'Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.' The scriptures illuminate our way, offering guidance and spiritual nourishment as we study them.

One profound way to find rich spiritual nourishment in the Old Testament is to look for Jesus Christ, the Bread of Life. Symbols like the manna, the sacrificial lamb, the brass serpent, and the prophet Jonah all point to Him, teaching us about His divine nature and mission.

Elder Dale G. Renlund encouraged us to 'remember and always focus on Jesus Christ.' By actively seeking Him in the Old Testament and in our daily lives, we can strengthen our faith and draw closer to Him, finding Him to be the ultimate treasure.

The Lord taught Adam that 'All things have their likeness, and all things are created and made to bear record of me.' By focusing on Jesus Christ, we can find deep meaning in the scriptures and increase our love for and faith in Him, recognizing His hand in all things.

It is significant to know that Jesus Christ is Jehovah in the Old Testament. President Dallin H. Oaks taught that scriptural references to 'God' or the 'Lord' are almost always the words of Jehovah, our risen Lord. This truth deepens our understanding of His eternal role.

When Jesus declared, 'Before Abraham was, I am,' He revealed His divine, pre-mortal existence as Jehovah. This statement shocked the listeners, highlighting the profound significance of His eternal identity and His role as the great 'I Am' before Abraham was, and indeed, before the world was.

The Lord planned to restore 'plain and precious things' taken from the Bible. Through Joseph Smith, He revealed additional scriptures like the book of Moses and the book of Abraham, restoring vital truths and accounts that enhance our understanding of God's dealings with His children.

The Bible and the Book of Mormon work together to make known the plain and precious things. As we study these sacred records, we gain a fuller witness of Jesus Christ and His gospel, receiving divine insights that strengthen our faith and testimony.

Restored accounts through Joseph Smith, such as Enoch’s city of Zion, Abraham’s vision of the council in heaven, and Melchizedek’s ministry, are 'plain and precious' because they reveal eternal truths and God's dealings with humanity. These accounts deepen our understanding of His plan and His love.
